text:
ashwin: Heads-up — saw a p95 regression on the /chat/fast-route canary starting ~14:03 UTC. Baseline was ~120ms, canary jumped to ~240ms for a subset of traffic :thinking:

maria: saw that too, but it looks concentrated on tier=pro routes with longer prompts. KV hit rate dropped from 92% to ~68% for those flows.

kevin: quick profiler dump shows a lot of kernel switch overhead when microbatch size is 1-2. We are triggering kernel selection twice per microbatch in the hot path.

jen: messy interaction: long prompts -> KV cache prefix mismatch -> smaller effective prefix reuse -> smaller microbatches -> kernel switchover overhead -> p95 spike. Feels like a cascade.

ashwin: (typo correction) ashwin: ^jen nailed it. I ran a flame graph; switching cost ~6-8ms per switch and we saw ~15 extra switches per request in worst cases.

sam: Can we bias queue policy to wait up to 8ms for same-route prefixes to accumulate? Proposed quick experiment: increase route-local hold window for tier=pro to 8ms and raise token_budget for that route from 40 -> 80 for canary.

maria: +1 for canary but let's be explicit with metrics and rollback criteria. Monitor p95, KV hit rate, kernel-switch-rate, microbatch-size-50/95/99, and overall throughput. If p95 > baseline + 30% for 5m, auto rollback.

kevin: config snippet for the canary (keep it minimal):
```json
{
  "route": "/chat/fast-route",
  "tier": "pro",
  "batching": {
    "local_hold_ms": 8,
    "token_budget": 80,
    "microbatch_prefer_homogeneous": true
  },
  "canary": {"weight": 0.15}
}
```

jen: also add a KV-prefetch heuristic: when prefix length > 64 tokens and kv_hit_rate < 85% in last 1m, issue a speculative prefetch for the next chunk. That should reduce early-cache-miss-driven microbatches.

ops-bot: deploy.canary started for /chat/fast-route tier=pro weight=15% by ashwin — tracking id cny-20260318-01 :rocket:

ashwin: running 15% canary now. Initial probe looks promising — p95 down to ~130ms after a warmup minute, KV hit climbing back to ~88%.

maria: nice. watch kernel-switch-rate closely — if it drops we'll be in good shape. Also check distribution of microbatch sizes, we want the 95th to move from 2 -> ~8.

kevin: preliminary numbers after 3m: p95=128ms, kv_hit=89%, kernel-switch-rate down 70%, microbatch-95=7. Throughput steady.

jen: great. schedule a gradual ramp to 40% over next 30m, keep the auto-rollback monitor. If we hit any regression, rollback to previous batching config.

sam: follow-up action: add a low-overhead metric for "kernel-switch-events" to tracing for next week so we can correlate with batch composition more easily.

maria: doc TODOs — add a short runbook for this cascade: detection -> quick canary config -> metrics to inspect -> rollback checklist. I'll PR to runtime playbooks.

ashwin: thanks team. I'll leave the canary to run and will post a post-canary summary in #eng-runtime when we hit 40% or rollback. :thumbsup:
